title: Microsoft Foundry: publish agents to the Microsoft 365 Copilot Agent Store without code
summary: The publishing capability, Azure consumption costs and Copilot Chat-only blocking limitation are supported by Microsoft documentation, and the rollout facts match the roadmap. Minor corrections should clarify where the approval path stops and acknowledge conflicting Microsoft descriptions of audience selection and REST publishing.

claims.claim: Developers can publish Foundry agents to Microsoft Copilot and Teams from the Foundry portal without constructing the package themselves.
claims.quote: Publishing from the portal calls Foundry's Microsoft 365 publish API and builds the Teams app package for you.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes direct, simplified no-code publishing of Azure AI Foundry agents to the Microsoft 365 Copilot Agent Store.
claims.quote: Developers can now publish Azure AI Foundry Agents directly to the Microsoft 365 Copilot Agent Store with a simplified, no-code experience.

claims.claim: The feature's Learn page uses the product name Microsoft Foundry.
claims.quote: When you publish a Microsoft Foundry agent to Microsoft Copilot and Teams, you and others can interact with and discover your agent through the Microsoft Copilot and Teams UI.

claims.claim: POST {{endpoint}}/agents/<agent-name>/microsoft365/publish?api-version=v1 is the documented Foundry REST publishing operation.

claims.fix: Keep the REST call. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/migrate-agent-applications, whose Path 3 says 'You can only publish through the Foundry portal—there's no public publish API.'
